benefits.details:
At Lodha, we prioritise the welfare of our employees and their families through our deeply ingrained "We Care" culture. Through our wellness initiatives, we nurture a culture where our employees can succeed in their careers while prioritising their personal lives, fostering a harmonious and fulfilling lifestyle for all.

benefits.details:
Lodha acknowledges the outstanding efforts of its associates through various prestigious awards.

benefits.name: Dietician & Creche - Wellness & Parental Support Benefits
benefits.details:
We understand and cater to the diverse needs of our workforce by implementing comprehensive policies that promote work-life balance and childcare support. Alongside maternity leave, we offer flexible working hours, travel assistance, and access to nutritious meals. Furthermore, we organise tailored learning sessions focused on health and well-being for our employees.

To enhance our support for working parents, we provide round-the-clock assistance through our service provider, offering valuable support, including access to doctors during late hours—an especially beneficial resource for young parents. Our commitment includes providing childcare support, such as a dedicated creche facility, to help our employees balance their professional responsibilities effectively. These initiatives underscore our dedication to creating an inclusive workplace where every individual can thrive both professionally and personally.

Our TACs conduct distinct final interviews and provide mentoring support, resulting in the right hiring decisions and reduced early attrition.

questions.question: HVAC How to calculate heat load
questions.answer: Calculating heat load involves assessing various factors to determine the heating or cooling requirements of a space.Identify the space dimensions (length, width, height) to calculate the volume.Consider the insulation properties of walls, windows, and roofs.Account for internal heat gains from occupants, equipment, and lighting.Use the formula: Q = U × A × ΔT, where Q is heat load, U is overall heat transfer coefficient, A is area, and ΔT is temperature difference.Example: For a room with 100 sq. ft. of window area, U-value of 0.5, and a ΔT of 20°F, Q = 0.5 × 100 × 20 = 1000 BTU/hr.

questions.question: How to measure subccolin and super heat
questions.answer: Subcooling and superheating are critical for HVAC efficiency, measured using temperature and pressure gauges.Subcooling is the process of cooling a liquid below its saturation temperature; measured using a thermometer at the condenser outlet.Superheat is the temperature of a vapor above its saturation point; measured at the evaporator outlet with a thermometer.Use a pressure gauge to determine the saturation temperature corresponding to the refrigerant pressure.For example, if the refrigerant pressure is 30 psi, the saturation temperature might be 40°F; if the actual temperature is 50°F, superheat is 10°F.Conversely, if the liquid refrigerant at the condenser is at 35°F but the saturation temperature is 45°F, subcooling is 10°F.
